newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds up to 102.56 before bears take over.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds up to 102.56 before bears take over.

text.p: September Bund futures on LIFFE are set for a bounce on Tuesday towards the 102.56 pivot level, technical analysts said.
But the market still looks shaky longer term and will likely slip back towards 101.42 retracement, they added.
"Bunds look like they're in a corrective frame of mind, they're still fairly oversold," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
"But in the longer term it looks like we're going down."
Diebel put initial resistance at 102.44, Monday's high, follwed by 102.56, a key intraday high from last Friday.
"If we start going through 102.56 we might have to review our outlook. That's the pivot level," said Diebel.
By 0700 GMT, September Bunds were up 0.13 at 102.28.
Diebel said the first major target on the downside was at 101.93, the 38.2 percent retracement of the prior upmove from 99.32 on May 29 to 103.52 on July 23.
"Beyond there we've got 101.42, the 50 percent pullback of that move," he added.
Tim Hampton, a salesman at the Royal Bank of Scotland, said Bunds were aiming for the hourly double top target at 101.74, in the middle of a large bank of support at 101.90/70.
"The view for the week remains to stay short of Bunds in small size, looking for a bounce below 102.00 for new highs next week," Hampton said in a note for clients.
"However, losses may accelerate again and although this is unlikely, new buyers should pay attention to the velocity of the move to 101.80."
By 0714 GMT, December Euromarks were up one basis points at 96.44.
